text: Writing clean code is an important skill for every programmer. Clean code is easy to read and understand, which saves time for everyone on the team. One key habit is following naming conventions: choose clear, meaningful names for variables and functions so their purpose is obvious. Another tip is to keep functions small and focused on a single task. This makes the code simpler to test and reuse. Finally, remember that clean code is much easier to maintain. When you return to your project months later, well-organised code helps you fix bugs and add new features without confusion.
